Name: 01_Sun
Title: The Sun
Narration: Our star: a ball of hydrogen and helium 1.39 million km across, holding 99.86% of all the mass in the Solar System. Everything on this tour orbits it. Its light takes 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth - you are always seeing the Sun as it was 8 minutes ago.

Name: 02_Mercury
Title: Mercury
Narration: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun: a year here lasts only 88 Earth days. With almost no atmosphere to hold heat, the surface swings from about 430 C in daylight to -180 C at night.

Name: 03_Venus
Title: Venus
Narration: Almost Earth's twin in size, but smothered in carbon dioxide at 92 times the air pressure at Earth's surface. The greenhouse effect makes it the hottest planet, around 465 C. It spins backwards and very slowly: one day on Venus is longer than its year.

Name: 04_Earth
Title: Earth
Narration: Home - the only world known to have life. Watch the line between day and night (the terminator) move as Earth turns once every 23 h 56 min. The tilt of its axis, 23.4 degrees, is what gives us seasons.

Name: 05_Moon
Title: The Moon
Narration: Earth's Moon, about 384,000 km away. It is tidally locked, so it always shows us the same face. The terrain here is real elevation data from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; the dark plains (maria) are ancient lava.

Name: 06_Mars
Title: Mars
Narration: The red planet, about half Earth's size; its colour is iron-oxide dust. Olympus Mons rises about 22 km - two and a half times Everest - and the Valles Marineris canyon is 4,000 km long. Elevation data: NASA Mars Global Surveyor.

Name: 07_Jupiter
Title: Jupiter
Narration: The largest planet: 318 times Earth's mass and 11 times its width. The Great Red Spot is a storm wider than Earth. Its four big moons were discovered by Galileo in 1610 and were the first objects seen orbiting another planet.

Name: 08_Saturn
Title: Saturn
Narration: Its rings are mostly water ice, about 280,000 km across but typically only tens of metres thick. Saturn is so light for its size that, on average, it is less dense than water.

Name: 09_Uranus
Title: Uranus
Narration: An ice giant tipped on its side: its axis is tilted 98 degrees, so each pole gets about 42 years of continuous sunlight followed by 42 years of darkness.

Name: 10_Neptune
Title: Neptune
Narration: The farthest planet, 30 times Earth's distance from the Sun; sunlight here is about 900 times fainter than at Earth. Its winds are the fastest measured in the Solar System, above 2,000 km/h.

Name: 11_LookBack
Title: Looking back at the Solar System
Narration: We are now 80 astronomical units (12 billion km) from the Sun, beyond Neptune's orbit. The Sun is just the brightest star in the sky, and its light takes 11 hours to get here. Sizes and distances on this tour are true to scale: the planets are specks lost in the dark.

Name: 12_MilkyWay
Title: The Milky Way
Narration: Our Sun is one of 100 to 400 billion stars in the Milky Way, a barred spiral galaxy about 100,000 light-years across. The marker shows the Sun, about 26,700 light-years from the centre, circling it at roughly 230 km/s - one lap takes about 230 million years.
